items.title: A formal algebraic space is affine exactly when its reduction is affine
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formal algebraic space over a scheme is an affine formal algebraic space if and only if its reduction is an affine scheme (statement lines 4017-4024). The proof establishes the two structural properties of the space that the criterion requires: by the two characterisation lemmas for the separated and quasi-compact types and the corresponding definitions, the space is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 4026-4029), and hence admits a presentation as a filtered colimit of thickenings of algebraic spaces by the structure theorem for such spaces (proof lines 4029-4032). Each member of that presentation has the same reduction as the space, so each is affine because a thickening of an affine algebraic space is affine; the presentation therefore exhibits the space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes with thickenings as transition maps, which is precisely the definition of an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 4032-4037). The claim is H2: the argument identifies the two hypotheses of the structure theorem, applies it, and then transfers affineness along the presentation, each step with its reason.
